name: Unakoti Heritage Site (Rock Carvings)
description: Ancient open-air gallery of colossal rock-cut sculptures and bas-reliefs of Hindu deities, primarily Shaivite, carved into the hillsides of Unakoti. Centerpiece is the ~30-foot Unakotiswara Kal Bhairava (Shiva head). Dates to 7th-9th century CE; UNESCO Tentative World Heritage Site since 2022. Also known as Subrai Khung.
facts: Name means 'one less than a crore' from local legend of 99,99,999 carvings
About 8 km east of Kailashahar, 178 km from Agartala
Annual Ashokastami Mela attracts thousands of pilgrims
ASI protected site with streams and forested setting

name: Kailashahar Town
description: District headquarters of Unakoti and historic former capital of the Tripuri kingdom. Gateway town on the banks of the Manu River near the Bangladesh border, serving as base for Unakoti rock carvings and local lakes/temples. Known for markets and as entry point to northern Tripura attractions.
facts: Headquarters of Unakoti district (formed 2012 from North Tripura)
Elevation around 28-32 metres
Nearest town to Unakoti site (~8 km)
Connected by road and near Kumarghat railway

name: Khowrabil Lake (Rajar Dighi)
description: Historic lake near Kailashahar in Unakoti district, popular for annual traditional water festival with boat races in October-November. Surrounded by scenic areas and close to Chaturdas Devata Mandir; draws visitors for water sports potential and natural setting.
facts: About 7 km from Kailashahar
Annual boat race during water festival
Also known as Rajar Dighi
Near Chaturdas Devata Mandir

name: Unakoti Eco Park
description: Developed eco-park adjacent to the Unakoti rock carvings site, offering walking trails, green spaces, and views of the forested hills and sculptures. Complements the heritage visit with nature relaxation amid the Unakoti landscape.
facts: Located near the entrance to Unakoti Heritage Site
Provides pathways and picnic spots
Part of tourism development around the rock carvings
Surrounded by lush vegetation and streams

name: Chaturdas Devata Mandir
description: Historic temple near Khowrabil Lake in Kailashahar area, linked to the ancient capital history of the region as per Rajmala texts. Attracts devotees and visitors exploring Unakoti district's spiritual sites.
facts: Close to Khowrabil Lake
Associated with ancient janapath history of Kailashahar
Part of local pilgrimage circuit
Mentioned in district tourism listings
